questions.question:
A company intends to allocate revenue across occurrences by using a recognition basis.  
  
Which recognition basis can be used?
questions.explanation:
Monthly is a recognition basis that distributes the revenue amount equally across the number of months specified by the occurrences. Actual start date and mid-month split are recognition-convention settings used to determine scheduling dates, and a revenue schedule is the configuration record. Microsoft’s migration guidance describes the revenue-recognition configuration as supporting occurrences by month or fiscal period.\
\

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company based in the United States uses Dynamics 365 Finance to collect and report sales tax. The company has a main account for every state in which it collects and reports sales tax.  
  
The system must automatically transfer each state's tax liability to its corresponding main account every month when the company runs the **Settle and post sales tax** process.  
  
You need to configure Dynamics 365 Finance.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a sales tax settlement period for each state.
Select a vendor account during the sales tax group setup.
Create a sales tax ledger posting group for each state. Associate a settlement account to a main account for vendor accounts in the vendor posting profile.
Create a sales tax authority for each state and associate the authority with the respective main account.

questions.explanation:
Sales tax ledger posting groups define the main accounts used to record and settle sales tax. The settle-and-post process offsets tax balances to the configured settlement account. When a tax authority is associated with a vendor, the settlement creates a vendor liability; the vendor posting profile maps that vendor transaction to its designated main account. Separate ledger posting groups and vendor-account posting-profile mappings therefore support automatic monthly settlement to a distinct main account for each state.

**Learn more:** [Set up Ledger posting groups for sales tax](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/general-ledger/tasks/set-up-ledger-posting-groups-sales-tax) · [Sales tax overview - Finance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/general-ledger/indirect-taxes-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 365 Finance and accepts customer payments in installments.  
  
You must configure the number of installments, the amount for each installment, and the due date for each installment in a payment schedule to determine the revenue allocation for each month. You must provide the total revenue amounts allocated over a period for a particular payment.  
  
You need to configure the system to allocate an invoice’s total outstanding amount.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: A payment schedule with a method of allocation set to Fixed amount.
A payment schedule with a method of allocation set to Total.

questions.explanation:
A payment schedule with the allocation method set to **Fixed amount** divides an invoice into installments with specified amounts and due dates. This supports allocating the invoice’s outstanding balance across the scheduled payments. The **Total** method makes the full outstanding invoice amount due rather than splitting it into fixed installment amounts.

**Learn more:** [Set up payment schedules with TDS allocation - Finance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/localizations/india/apac-ind-tds-payment-schedule-setup-with-tds-allocation)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A customer uses Dynamics 365 Finance to manage its budgets.  
  
You review the customer's budget funds available calculation and find that budget amounts posted two weeks earlier are not included in the budget control check on a purchase order.  
  
You confirm that budget control is set to active.  
  
You need to determine why the budget posted two weeks ago is not being reflected correctly.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Verify that available budget funds are configured appropriately.
Post a budget transfer to add the correct funds.
Verify whether budget plans are still in draft status.
Compare the budget control active date to the date of the posted register entries to verify that it was active at the time of posting.

questions.explanation:
Budget register entries posted before budget control was turned on are not considered by budget control. Comparing the budget control active date with the dates of the posted register entries establishes whether those amounts were posted while budget control was active and therefore eligible to affect the purchase-order budget check.

**Learn more:** [Budget control overview - Finance | Dynamics 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/budgeting/budget-control-overview-configuration)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 365 Finance.

1. Select the items to defer by default.  
2. Configure the deferred items for sales order transaction types.

You need to update the configuration so that the transaction lines are deferred as required.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Set up deferred items for Purchasing transaction types.

Select the Account relation for all items.

A company uses Dynamics 365 Finance.  
  
The company needs expense invoices to be approved at the line level.  
  
You need to enter the expense invoice in the system so that workflow approval can occur at the line level.  
  
Which vendor invoice method should you use?
questions.explanation:
Dynamics 365 Finance vendor invoice workflow can require review at the invoice header, invoice line, or both. Pending vendor invoices are created and maintained as unposted vendor invoices and can be submitted to the vendor invoice workflow, enabling line-level approval.\
\
**Learn more:** [Vendor invoices overview - Finance | Dynamics 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/accounts-payable/vendor-invoices-overview)

questions.domain: Implement and manage accounts payable and expenses
questions.question:
You are implementing Dynamics 365 Finance.  
  
You must configure a more precise cash flow forecast for sales tax. The sales tax calculation must be based on anticipated transaction amounts and dates.  
  
You need to configure the cash flow forecast. Which setup should you use?
questions.explanation:
Dependent accounts create forecast amounts in a related main account as a percentage of cash-flow amounts forecast for a primary main account. This supports forecasting the sales-tax cash-flow effect from the expected underlying transaction amounts and timing.\
\
**Learn more:** [Cash flow forecasting - Finance | Dynamics 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/cash-bank-management/cash-flow-forecasting)
